To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

feeding difficulties can be measured using a questionnaire that can be completed in a reasonable amount of time, that the questionnaire is reliable and can be used to assess the level of feeding difficulty of patients with dementia and that the questionnaire can also be used as an evaluation tool to monitor the effect of intervention on feeding difficulty.

feeding difficulty is not a unitary construct; it is possible to identify three factors which are associated with feeding difficulty; and these three factors are patient obstinacy, nursing intervention and indicator of feeding difficulty.
the feeding difficulties in patients with dementia are caused by the patients' obstinacy or lack of cooperation, the nursing staff's intervention and the patients' physical and mental state.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a multidimensional analysis of feeding difficulty.
the development of a new instrument to assess the feeding difficulties experienced by elderly people with dementia.
the development and application of a new instrument to measure feeding difficulty in elderly people with dementia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
(1) the three factors are independent of each other and (2) that each factor is a valid and reliable indicator of feeding difficulty in patients.
the feeding problems of patients with dementia are not only related to their physical and mental condition but also to the nursing staff and the way they intervene in the feeding process.

the feeding difficulty of patients with dementia is related to their obstinacy and/or passivity, to the amount of nursing intervention and to indicators of feeding difficulty such as the patient's ability to chew and swallow.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the three factors of the questionnaire are independent of each other, and that the three factors together are related to feeding problems.
the feeding difficulty of elderly people with dementia can be assessed by a questionnaire that is easy to use and that can be completed in a short time.
the feeding difficulty of patients with dementia is a multidimensional construct, which can be measured by means of a questionnaire administered to the nursing staff.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the questionnaire can be used as a tool to identify the most common types of feeding problems in elderly people with dementia.
the feeding difficulty of patients with dementia can be assessed by means of a short questionnaire, which can be administered to nursing staff.
feeding problems in elderly people with dementia are not only related to the severity of dementia but also to nursing interventions.
